items.title: Tom Hanks Returns As David S. Pumpkins For ‘Saturday Night Live’ Opener — Interrupted By Donald Trump’s Fear Of A Midterm Ass-Whipping
items.summary:
Tom Hanks put the pumpkin suit back on this weekend, reprising David S. Pumpkins in the cold open of Saturday Night Live's Halloween episode. The sketch didn't stay his for long: James Austin Johnson's Donald Trump broke in partway through to deliver a closing midterm pitch to viewers, with the election set for Tuesday.

The setup was the same one that made the character a recurring joke a decade ago. A couple rides through a haunted attraction, Pumpkins pops out in his cheap black-and-orange suit flanked by two dancing skeletons, and nobody can figure out what he is supposed to be. Hanks first played the part just weeks before Trump's 2016 win, a coincidence the sketch leaned on directly. "We both appeared in 2016," Johnson's Trump said. "We're both very loud, very orange, and very frankly annoying, but we love Tom Hanks."

From there the sketch, as Deadline described it, worked through the odder corners of Trump's late campaign rhetoric. Johnson's Trump conceded bad polling — "The midterms are on Tuesday, and the polls say we're doing very badly" — and warned that Texas was turning purple, "just like my hands." He also kept circling back to admiring men's bodies, a bit drawn from the president's recent remarks about Sen. Jon Husted, who is defending his Ohio seat against Democrat Sherrod Brown.

The Texas Senate race got its own stretch, with Johnson's Trump grudgingly endorsing Ken Paxton over Democrat James Talarico while insulting him throughout. Republicans have put significant money behind Paxton, whose corruption scandals have left the contest a tossup. Hanks held his freeze-frame pose through most of it.

Two supporting cameos rounded out the open. Saidah Belo-Osagie played Nicki Minaj, who has been turning up at Trump rallies and was floated in the sketch as a future press secretary, and Veronika Slowikowska appeared as Katie Zacharia, whose real stint as press secretary ran less than a week. Zacharia had publicly said she hoped Scarlett Johansson would play her.

items.title: Michael Mann Accidentally Shoots Himself at Firing Range: Report
items.summary:
Director Michael Mann accidentally shot himself in the leg at a Los Angeles shooting range on Saturday, according to a report from TMZ picked up by Consequence. An ambulance took him to a local hospital for treatment.

The incident reportedly happened at The Range LA at around 4 p.m. local time. Mann was holstering his firearm when it discharged, per the report.

No further details on his condition have been reported, and Mann has not commented publicly.

items.title: Harry Styles Wraps Up MSG Residency With Pizza Rat Costume, “Psycho Killer” Cover, Jalen Brunson
items.summary:
Harry Styles closed out his 30-night run at Madison Square Garden on Halloween, capping the stand with a costume, a cover and a banner presentation from a Knick. The final show fell on October 31, which let Styles revive Harryween, the Halloween concert tradition he started during his 2021 residency at the same building.

For the last night, Styles dressed as Pizza Rat, the New York City subway rodent of viral fame, and later changed into an "I Am a Rat" T-shirt. Zoë Kravitz, his fiancée, attended as a bodega plastic bag. Stereogum noted the pairing as a fairly complete piece of city iconography.

Knicks guard Jalen Brunson handed Styles a banner marking the 30-show residency, and appeared to be in costume himself — running gear, a baseball cap and headphones, the outfit Styles has been wearing on his walks across the Williamsburg Bridge.

Musically, the night brought a debut: a cover of Talking Heads' "Psycho Killer." It follows other nods to the band on this tour, including a snippet of "This Must Be The Place (Naive Melody)" worked into "Treat People With Kindness."

The Friday show leaned on a different set of costumes. Styles appeared as '70s-era Elvis and then as his own teenage self auditioning for The X Factor, performing Stevie Wonder's "Isn't She Lovely" — the song he sang at that audition. He also took a moment that night to complain about what New York charges for caffeinated drinks.

The residency more than doubles the 15-date MSG stand he played four years ago, when Harryween began.
